title: Finite flat Hom-complex model with arbitrary scalar-extension comparison
statement:
Let $R\to S$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Work in ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and derived Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. Let $K,L\in D(S)$ be pseudo-coherent over $S$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], and assume that $L$ has finite Tor amplitude over $R$: there are integers $a\le b$ such that $H^i(L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every $R$-module $N$ and every $i\notin[a,b]$. There exist a bounded-above complex $P^\bullet$ of finite free $S$-modules representing $K$, and a bounded complex $F^\bullet$ representing $L$, whose terms are $R$-flat finitely presented $S$-modules. Here a module is $R$-flat when tensoring with it preserves exact sequences; finitely presented means admitting a presentation $S^m\to S^n\to F^j\to0$ with $m,n$ finite. For any such choices the Hom complex $E^\bullet=\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(P^\bullet,F^\bullet)$, with $E^n=\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}_S(P^i,F^{i+n})$ and differential $d(h)=d_Fh-(-1)^nhd_P$, is bounded below, has $R$-flat finitely presented $S$-modules as terms, and represents $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(K,L)$ in $D(S)$. For every ring map $R\to T$, put $S_T=S\otimes_RT$, $K_T=K\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}S_T$, and $L_T=L\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}S_T$. The termwise tensors $P^\bullet\otimes_RT$ and $F^\bullet\otimes_RT$ represent $K_T$ and $L_T$, respectively. There is an isomorphism in $D(S_T)$
$$E^\bullet\otimes_RT\ \simeq\ R\operatorname{Hom}_{S_T}(K_T,L_T),$$
where the tensor on the left is ordinary termwise tensor. This is represented by the chain isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(P,F)\otimes_RT\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{S_T}^\bullet(P\otimes_RT,F\otimes_RT),\qquad(h\otimes t)(p\otimes u)=h(p)\otimes tu.$$
Under $H^0(E^\bullet)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S)}(K,L)$, the map on classes defined by tensoring degree-zero cocycles sends a morphism to its derived scalar extension $K_T\to L_T$. The comparisons respect identity and iterated ring extension and are natural in derived morphisms of $K,L$. No flatness of $R\to T$ or Noetherianity is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0E1U, lemma-compute-RHom-relatively-perfect, (a), (b), and its finite-presentation clause; cocycle normalization and iterated-extension compatibility from the termwise Hom identification in its proof.

proof.text: Choose bounded-above finite free $S$-complexes $P,Q$ representing $K,L$, using pseudo-coherence. Since $S$ is $R$-flat, each $Q^i$, as a finite direct sum of copies of $S$, is $R$-flat. By the bounded-above-flat K-flatness lemma, $Q\otimes_R N$ computes $L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N$ for every $R$-module $N$ (using the singleton-site comparison for ordinary derived tensor). It is therefore exact in degree $a-1$ for every $N$. The flat-opcycles criterion gives $R$-flatness of $C=\operatorname{coker}(Q^{a-1}\to Q^a)$. Set $F^a=C$, $F^i=Q^i$ for $i>a$, and $F^i=0$ for $i<a$, with induced differential. This is a bounded complex: $Q$ was bounded above. Taking $N=R$ gives $H^i(Q)=0$ below $a$, so the quotient map $Q\to F$ induces isomorphisms on all cohomology groups. Thus $F$ represents $L$. The displayed presentation $Q^{a-1}\to Q^a\to C\to0$ is finite free, and the other nonzero terms are finite free. Hence all terms of $F$ are finitely presented over $S$.

source.place: Tag 0E1U, lemma-compute-RHom-relatively-perfect, first paragraph; Tag 0DHV, lemma-structure-relatively-perfect, (1) implies (2); Tag 0653, lemma-last-one-flat.

proof.text: Now take any choices $P,F$ as in the statement. Choose integers $u,v,w$ with $P^i=0$ for $i>u$ and $F^j=0$ for $j\notin[v,w]$. In degree $n$, only indices $v-n\leq i\leq\min(u,w-n)$ contribute to the product total Hom of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]; this is a finite set. Thus the product is the displayed finite direct sum, and it is zero when $n<v-u$. If $P^i\cong S^{r_i}$, its summand is $(F^{i+n})^{r_i}$. Tensoring an injection of $R$-modules with this finite sum is a finite sum of injections, so the term is $R$-flat. Direct sums of the given finite presentations, repeated $r_i$ times, give a finite presentation over $S$. The Hom differential is the one in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0E1U, lemma-compute-RHom-relatively-perfect, proof of (a), finite direct sum calculation and final finite-presentation clause.

proof.text: Finite free modules are projective (a free module is a direct summand of itself). The complex $F$ is bounded, in particular bounded below. Hence [lem-sc-affine-projective-complex-derived-hom], applied over $S$ to the bounded-above projective complex $P$ and the bounded-below complex $F$, says that $\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(P,F)$, with terms $\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_S(P^i,F^{i+n})$, represents $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(K,L)$ of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site with ring $S$. This is exactly the derived Hom of the statement, so $Q_S\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(P,F)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_S(K,L)$ in $D(S)$. This gives the asserted derived representative for every choice, not just for the truncation constructed in step 1.

source.place: Tag 0A66, lemma-RHom-out-of-projective, as used in Tag 0E1U, proof of (a).

proof.text: Both $P$ and $F$ are bounded above and termwise $R$-flat, so they are K-flat over $R$. For either $G=P$ or $G=F$, apply [lem-sfb-flat-algebra-derived-module-tensor-exchange] with $N=T$. After restriction to $D(S)$ it identifies $Q_SG\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}(S\otimes_RT)$ with the mixed tensor using a free $R$-resolution of $T$. Since $G$ is $R$-K-flat, tensoring its augmentation gives a quasi-isomorphism from that mixed tensor to $G\otimes_RT$. The canonical derived-to-ordinary comparison is formed from an $S$-K-flat resolution $V\to G$: the map $V\otimes_SS_T\to G\otimes_SS_T$ is $S_T$-linear. Its restriction is the cited augmentation comparison under the balancing $(g\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto sg\otimes t$. Its restriction to $S$ is the cited comparison. Forgetting an $S_T$-complex to an $S$-complex preserves its kernels, images and cohomology; therefore this comparison is a quasi-isomorphism in $D(S_T)$ as well. Consequently $P_T=P\otimes_RT$ and $F_T=F\otimes_RT$ represent $K_T,L_T$, without any flatness assumption on $T$.

source.place: Tag 0661, lemma-base-change-comparison; Tag 0E1U, lemma-compute-RHom-relatively-perfect, proof of (b).

proof.text: Apply the half-bounded Hom scalar-isomorphism lemma to the ring map $S\to S_T$, source $P$, and target $F$. The ordinary balancing isomorphism $M\otimes_SS_T\cong M\otimes_RT$, $m\otimes(s\otimes t)\mapsto sm\otimes t$, turns its chain isomorphism into the asserted $\chi:E\otimes_RT\to\operatorname{Hom}_{S_T}^\bullet(P_T,F_T)$. Its formula becomes $(\chi(h\otimes t))(p\otimes u)=h(p)\otimes tu$. The lemma assumes finite free terms and an upper bound for $P$ and a lower bound for $F$, which hold here; it assumes no flatness of $S_T$ over $S$. Equivalently, each term is a finite sum of the basis identifications $(F^{i+n})^{r_i}\otimes_RT\cong(F^{i+n}\otimes_RT)^{r_i}$.

source.place: Tag 0E1U, lemma-compute-RHom-relatively-perfect, proof of (b), last displayed equality; Tag 0ATK, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism, finite-support calculation.

proof.text: The complex $P_T$ is bounded above finite free over $S_T$. The complex $F_T$ is bounded. Apply [lem-sc-affine-projective-complex-derived-hom] over $S_T$ to $P_T,F_T$, and use step 4. Composing this derived-category isomorphism with the localization of the chain isomorphism in step 5 gives $Q_{S_T}(E\otimes_RT)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_{S_T}(K_T,L_T)$. This uses ordinary termwise tensor on $E$. It requires no K-flatness assertion for the bounded-below complex $E$.

source.place: Tag 0E1U, lemma-compute-RHom-relatively-perfect, proof of (b); Tag 0A66, lemma-RHom-out-of-projective.

proof.text: A degree-zero Hom cocycle $h$ is precisely a chain map $P\to F$. A degree-zero boundary is $d_Fs+sd_P$ for a degree-minus-one cochain $s$, so quotienting cocycles by boundaries is quotienting chain maps by homotopy. The projective-source morphism-representative lemma identifies this quotient with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S)}(K,L)$. Under $\chi$, the cocycle $h\otimes1$ is the chain map $h\otimes_R1:P_T\to F_T$. By the natural augmentation comparisons of step 4 this represents the derived scalar extension of $h$. Tensoring the equation $h-h'=d_Fs+sd_P$ tensors its homotopy too, so the map on classes is well-defined and has the asserted normalization.

source.place: Tag 0E1U, lemma-compute-RHom-relatively-perfect, termwise identification; Tag 0A66 and the degree-zero Hom differential. Cocycle normalization written out by Q104.

proof.text: To check target naturality for a derived morphism $L\to L'$ between allowed targets represented by $F,F'$, choose a bounded-above finite free $Q$ representing $L$. The morphism-representative lemma supplies chain maps $q:Q\to F$ and $r:Q\to F'$ representing the chosen isomorphism to $L$ and the given morphism; $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Choose $c$ at most the lower Tor bound for $L$ and the lower support bounds of $F,F'$. The step-1 argument with $c$ gives a bounded $R$-flat finitely presented complex $B=\tau_{\geq c}Q$. Both maps descend to $B$: at degree $c$, $q^cd_Q^{c-1}=d_Fq^{c-1}=0$, and likewise for $r$, because both targets vanish below $c$. Hence $F\leftarrow B\to F'$ represents the morphism with a quasi-isomorphism on the left. The complexes $B,F$ are $R$-K-flat, so [lem-pc-mixed-tensor-kflat-quasi-iso](i), with second complex $T[0]$, makes the left arrow a quasi-isomorphism after tensoring with $T$. This also proves independence of the chosen bounded flat target representative by taking the morphism to be an identity.

source.place: Tag 0DHV, lemma-structure-relatively-perfect, good truncation construction; Tag 0653, lemma-last-one-flat; Tag 064L, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side. Target-roof refinement written out by Q104.

proof.text: The formula for $\chi$ commutes with precomposition and postcomposition of chain maps: both orders send $h\otimes t$ and $p\otimes u$ to the same value, and tensoring preserves homotopies. Every derived source morphism between the chosen bounded-above finite free representatives is represented by a chain map, by the morphism-representative lemma. Every derived target morphism is represented by the roof of step 8. Applying the comparisons of [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model], natural covariantly in the target, before and after extension shows that the quasi-isomorphism in that roof remains a quasi-isomorphism on Hom complexes; the derived identifications of steps 3 and 6 are those of [lem-sc-affine-projective-complex-derived-hom], whose targets in the roof are all bounded. Thus chain-level naturality extends to these roofs and gives naturality in all derived morphisms and all choices. For $R\to T\to U$, each $F^j\otimes_RT$ is $T$-flat: tensoring a $T$-module injection with it is tensoring the underlying $R$-injection with $F^j$. Its finite $S_T$-presentation is obtained by tensoring the given finite presentation, using right exactness. The same injection test shows $S_T$ is $T$-flat. A finite polynomial presentation of $S$ over $R$ tensors to one of $S_T$ over $T$. The finite free complexes $P_T,Q_T$ (with $Q$ from step 1) witness pseudo-coherence of $K_T,L_T$, and bounded $T$-flatness of $F_T$ gives finite Tor amplitude by bounded-flat K-flatness. Hence the repeated construction is defined. Under the tensor associators, direct and repeated comparisons both evaluate $(h\otimes t)\otimes u$ on $(p\otimes t')\otimes u'$ as $h(p)\otimes (tt')uu'$, with $tt'$ mapped to $U$. For $T=R$ the formula is the identity. This proves identity and iteration compatibility.
